out.rationale: The authors say they mainly follow Burns et al.'s original setup and state what they add (harmlessness target, explicit and implicit conflicts, preference optimization), which is EXTENDS. They use the extension to argue that weak-to-strong success can hide selective misalignment, but they do not dispute Burns et al.'s generalization result.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Weak-to-strong supervision protocol; the extension adds conflicting objectives (a harmfulness reward or helpful data) and studies which knowledge regions are sacrificed

text: The authors mainly follow the weak-to-strong setup of Burns et al. (2024), including its reward modeling task, across models of different sizes. They extend it by making harmlessness the target, adding explicit or implicit conflicting objectives, and adding a preference-optimization variant to probe weak-to-strong deception.
title: Yang et al. extend Burns et al.'s weak-to-strong setup with conflicting alignment objectives
